problems.heading: Useful communication starts with context, trust and practical delivery.
problems.intro: Aboriginal and regional organisations often work across community priorities, funding requirements, remote delivery and multiple audiences. Marketing should make that work easier to understand without flattening culture, community ownership or local context.

items.title: Complex audiences
items.text: Community members, funders, government, customers and partners may all need different information from the same organisation.

items.title: Remote access
items.text: Websites and digital systems need to work on mobile devices, slower connections and across dispersed communities.

items.title: Funding pressure
items.text: Applications, reporting and business plans need clear evidence, structure and language that reflects the organisation’s actual work.

items.title: Cultural IP
items.text: Stories, images, names and cultural knowledge need agreed permissions, attribution and boundaries before they are used in marketing.

system.heading: Listen first. Agree the boundaries. Then build what is useful.
system.intro: We do not claim cultural authority. Project protocols, approvals, language, imagery and intellectual-property boundaries are agreed with the organisation and relevant knowledge holders before publication.

steps.title: Listen
steps.text: Understand the organisation, community priorities, audiences, approvals, funding context and what success actually means.

steps.title: Scope
steps.text: Agree what can be shared, who approves it, what must stay private and how cultural and intellectual property will be handled.

steps.title: Build
steps.text: Create the website, communications, campaign, e-commerce, booking or reporting system in plain language and practical formats.

steps.title: Deliver remotely
steps.text: Support projects from Darwin with online collaboration and planned regional or remote travel where the engagement requires it.

steps.title: Hand over
steps.text: Provide clear files, guidance and systems your team can keep using, with ongoing support available when needed.

proof.heading: Commercial results, not decorative metrics.
proof.note: Selected results from prior marketing roles and campaign experience. Results vary by business, market, budget and offer; these figures are not guarantees of future performance.

niches.heading: Built to support Aboriginal organisations and remote communities.
niches.primaryText: Aboriginal corporations, community-controlled health and service organisations, art centres, ranger groups, community stores, tourism operators, bush-food enterprises and other community-led organisations.

offer.heading: Tell us what your organisation needs to communicate, fund or grow.
offer.intro: We begin by understanding the audience, approvals, delivery environment and internal capacity. From there, we agree a clear scope rather than pushing a standard package.
offer.priceNote: Scopes are agreed before work starts. Remote delivery, travel requirements and third-party costs are quoted separately where relevant.

national.heading: Based in Darwin. Supporting the Top End, Central Australia and organisations across Australia.
national.text: Most work can be delivered remotely. Where a project benefits from being on Country or in community, travel can be scoped in advance. We do not claim offices outside Darwin and we do not present remote communities as generic service areas.

items.question: Do you work with Aboriginal corporations and community-controlled organisations?
items.answer: Yes. GT Marketing can support websites, digital communications, campaigns, e-commerce and booking systems, funding communications and practical marketing systems. Scope, approvals and cultural protocols are agreed with the organisation before work begins.

items.question: Can you work with organisations in remote communities?
items.answer: Yes. Projects can be delivered remotely from Darwin, with low-bandwidth and mobile access considered in the design. Where in-person work is useful, travel can be scoped separately.

items.question: Do you provide grant and funding support?
items.answer: GT Marketing can support the communication and presentation of grant applications, funding submissions, reports and business plans, including structure, evidence presentation and plain-language writing. Eligibility, legal, financial and specialist grant advice remains with the organisation and its advisers.

items.question: How do you handle cultural stories, images and intellectual property?
items.answer: GT Marketing does not assume permission to use cultural material. The organisation determines approvals, attribution, access restrictions and what can or cannot be published. These boundaries are documented in the project scope.
